text:
maria_cs: FYI — SkyBridge reported a reproducible issue with the rerank endpoint. When they send batched rerank requests (batch_size > 1) the returned ranking order is nondeterministic for the same input set. Impacting search relevance in production. Customer sees different orderings between repeated identical requests. They want an ETA and possible workaround. :exclamation:

jamal_eng: can you paste repro steps + an example payload? is this through the REST API or our SDK? which model variant?

maria_cs: REST API, model: redwood-rerank-v1 (customer says 'redwood-rr-1' in their notes). Repro steps we got from them: 
1) Prepare 8 candidate docs (ids attached below) 
2) Call POST /v1/rerank with batch of 8 candidates (single request) and same query twice in a row 
3) Observe order differs between the two responses ~40% of the time

Sample payload they provided: 
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "redwood-rerank-v1",
  "query": "best enterprise inference platform for latency-sensitive workloads",
  "candidates": ["doc_1","doc_2","doc_3","doc_4","doc_5","doc_6","doc_7","doc_8"],
  "batch_size": 8,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

Observed responses (two repeated calls, identical payload):
- run A ordering: [doc_2, doc_5, doc_1, doc_7, doc_3, doc_4, doc_6, doc_8]
- run B ordering: [doc_5, doc_2, doc_1, doc_7, doc_3, doc_4, doc_6, doc_8]

alex_sales: customer escalation risk. They flagged this as blocking a go-live next week if we can't provide a mitigation. Sales asks for a short-term workaround and ETA to fix.

anita_pm: quick clarification: is this guaranteed nondeterminism or appears only under certain conditions? also need to decide whether this is block for roadmap (rerank reliability) vs. lower priority. Acceptance criteria from product: reproducible test-case, root cause identified (serving vs model), fix + unit/regression tests, rollout gating to avoid regressions.

jamal_eng: initial questions from eng: 1) Is cache or batching reordering tokens across internal shards? 2) Does this correlate with quantized vs FP model builds? 3) Need exact request IDs and timestamps to pull traces. maria_cs can you attach the two request ids customer logged?

maria_cs: they provided request IDs and brief logs: 
- req: sb-2026-03-18-9981 (run A)
- req: sb-2026-03-18-9982 (run B)
They also noted it reproduces more often when traffic is medium-high and when region = us-west2. Batch_size=8 in their test, temperature=0.0.

sre-bot: pulled traces for sb-2026-03-18-9981 & 9982. Attachments: trace 7f9a2c (service: rerank-svc, backend: rerank-worker-12). No worker OOMs, latency spikes around 220–260ms.

jamal_eng: thanks — i'll try to reproduce locally with redwood-rerank-v1 using identical payload and batch size. Quick hypothesis: there might be nondeterministic tie-break ordering in the reranker scoring layer when scores are equal up to float rounding. If so, we should make ordering deterministic (stable sort by score + doc_id).

anita_pm: if that's the cause, acceptance criteria should require stable deterministic ordering for identical scores and a regression test with the customer's candidate set. Also we need a rollout plan: patch -> canary -> production for rerank-svc.

alex_sales: customer asks: can they force single-item reranking as workaround? they prefer something we can do ASAP.

jamal_eng: temporary workarounds: 1) Split batch into single requests (higher QPS/cost) — works but not ideal 2) Add secondary tie-break on client side using doc_id — only viable if client controls final UI ordering. We can ship server-side fix quickly if root cause is stable-sort bug.

maria_cs: customer confirms they can try single-request fallback, but they want us to prioritize server fix. They've agreed to provide a small candidate set (the 8 ids above) to reproduce.

jamal_eng: creating engineering ticket INF-8273, assigning to rerank team. Priority: P1 for customer impact, but marking P2 internally until we confirm root cause. Will update with a minimal repro branch and unit test.

anita_pm: adding to product backlog under rerank reliability. Launch criteria: deterministic output for identical inputs, regression test added, doc update for batch semantics. Please include rollout playbook (canary criteria and rollback steps).

maria_cs: noted. i'll post the customer's minimal candidate set and accept sign-off when ENG provides a staging patch. :thumbsup:

tracebot: created ticket INF-8273 and linked traces 7f9a2c.

jamal_eng: next steps for eng: reproduce locally w/ provided IDs, confirm if stable-sort fixes it, open PR with regression test. target: initial triage + reproducer within 48 hours.

maria_cs: passing this to customer and will update thread once they try single-request fallback.

alex_sales: please keep me posted — i'll relay timeline to the customer.

anita_pm: thanks everyone.
